schema_version: v0 — skill-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
axis: orientation — a GATHER, not a decision. It reads the world and hands back a shape; it casts nothing, builds nothing, and resolves nothing on its own authority.
what: The standing answer to the question Akien asks most often. Four gathers in a FIXED order — RULINGS (bin/cmd/recordverdict, bare, lists the gate), ALARMS (bin/cmd/slate for live troubles, bin/cmd/probescan for feedback paths, bin/cmd/test -q for the proof corpus), QUESTIONS (CairnCommons/questions/), THE SLATE (bin/cmd/slate) — then ONE overview, then ONE question at a time until he stops. The order is the content: rulings come first because they are the bulk of what he is asking for, and CC keeps putting them last.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM, measured 2026-08-12 in the session that bore this. Akien asked 'do we have open questions or alarms we should tackle first?' and CC led with questions and alarms, spent twelve tool calls, and reported the 104 findings standing at his gate as an aside in the middle. His correction, verbatim: 'when i ask what's left to do, getting those 105 rulings done are a big part of what i'm asking for, and you are asking me about the questions first.' The gather was not wrong — the ORDER was, and an order that lives in CC's judgment is re-derived (differently) every time. Second symptom, his words: 'we're creating a shortcut for my monkey. the habit machine that a human is.' A skill he can reach for by reflex costs one word; the same gather assembled by hand costs a session's attention and comes out in a different order each time.
invoke: /whatslefttodo — no arguments. It is deliberately parameterless: the subject IS 'what's left to do', and the four gathers ARE that subject's answer-shape.
deliberate_redundancy: THIS SKILL IS A THIN ALIAS FOR `/reorient to rulings, then alarms, then questions, then the slate` AND THAT IS RULED, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Akien, 2026-08-12, verbatim: 'i agree that /whatslefttodo is a silly redundant version of /reorient to rulings, then alarms, then questions, then the slate --- but we're creating a shortcut for my monkey. the habit machine that a human is. if i create the habit around that, we're better off, even if all that's in the skill is "/reorient to rulings, then alarms, then questions, then the slate and then answer: what's left to do, with an overview, and then one question at a time."' THE DISTINGUISHER, because CC proposed killing this exact skill as near-synonym drift the same morning it was ruled: the anti-coinage rule governs the SYSTEM's vocabulary, where a near-duplicate term costs Akien a hunt. It does not govern AKIEN'S HAND, where a memorable name buys a reflex and the reflex is the entire product. The test is WHO TYPES IT. Expect the urge to simplify this away to recur; this field is the answer.
for_whom: AKIEN, and specifically his habit machine — the skill exists so the gather is one keystroke instead of a re-derivation. Secondarily CC, who gets the order settled as structure rather than re-deciding it each session (Law 1).

input_contract.rulings: THE FIRST GATHER, and first because it is the bulk of what he is asking for. An object {ran, count, oldest_id}: `ran` is the command actually run (`bin/cmd/recordverdict`, bare), `count` is how many findings stand at Akien's gate, `oldest_id` is the id of the oldest one. THE ID RATHER THAN THE AGE, deliberately: a count can be copied off the session-open banner and an id cannot — it exists only in the list, and the list exists only in the instrument. The door re-reads `learning_block.pending_findings` at the instant of firing and refuses a mismatch, which is the half of this charter's tracked debt that presence alone could never catch.
input_contract.alarms: THE SECOND GATHER, three instruments. An object {ran, live_troubles, probes, proofs}: `ran` names all three commands (`bin/cmd/slate`, `bin/cmd/probescan`, `bin/cmd/test -q`), `live_troubles` is the LIST OF IDS still live — the set, not a count, because Law 9 says an old trouble is not stale by age and naming them is what lets a reader check 'still live' — and `probes`/`proofs` carry what probescan and test reported. The door re-reads the trouble lane and refuses a mismatched set. It does NOT re-run probescan or the proof corpus: minutes-long judges get routed around, so those two ride operator-reported and are checked for presence only. That is the residue, named rather than assumed.
input_contract.questions: THE THIRD GATHER — the corpus that is the resolver for design DETAILS, reached for before reaching for Akien. An object {ran, open}: `ran` is the census command, `open` is how many `open-*` questions are unresolved. The door re-reads the open lane through `bin/cmd/slate`'s own reader and refuses a mismatch. It is HALF the lane by construction: the charters' `filed_edges` need a projector that does not exist yet (open-the-frontier-projector), and reporting the homeless half as the whole lane is the cropped map that ruling was made against.
input_contract.slate: THE FOURTH GATHER, last. An object {ran, slate_id}: the command, and the id of the slate the render actually chose. The door re-reads it by CALLING `bin/cmd/slate`'s `_newest_slate` rather than globbing — that ranking (date, then written_at, then filename) carries two measured corrections in its own docstring, and a second copy of it here would be the Law 1 defect at the smallest possible scale.
input_contract.overview: THE ONE SYNTHESIS across all four — counts with their ages, reds with their evidence, and CC's read of what the order should be. A RECOMMENDATION, NEVER A MENU (the charter's falsifier reds on a menu), and it names what only Akien can answer versus what CC should resolve itself. Required in substance: what this field is for is that the gather ends in a position, and a gather that ends in a list has handed the work back to the person who asked.
input_contract.bullets: the exit-time finding — a list of {text, stratum} with stratum in code|tree, standing at Akien's gate. What this firing LEARNED that he should see. This is also where the skill's own falsifier gets its denominator: when he answers 'you asked me about X first', that verdict is the reordering the charter's `how_it_learns` is waiting for, and it arrives as a training pair instead of as a sentence in a chat.
input_contract.exit: routed_forward when the four gathers ran and the overview was given; routed_out when a gather could not complete — an instrument that would not run is a result to report, never a silent green (Law 9). Both exits berth and both emit their finding.

writes_to: TWO INSTANCE-SPACE ARTIFACTS AND NOTHING IN THE COMMONS. Since 2026-08-12 it is tenant #5 of the `cairn.machines.skill_block` seam: a firing berths under `~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths/whatslefttodo/` and emits its finding to Akien's gate. Both die with the box, which is right — the gather is a reading of the world at an instant, not knowledge. It still files NOTHING to the commons and casts nothing: every write it might motivate happens through the door that owns it — a verdict through `cairn recordverdict`, a node through /idea -> /intent -> /sorted, a boundary through /saveslate.
how_it_learns: ITS FEEDBACK IS AKIEN'S REORDERING, and since 2026-08-12 that feedback ARRIVES AS A TRAINING PAIR instead of as a sentence in a chat. Every firing emits a finding to his gate; when he answers 'you asked me about X first', that is a verdict against a traced firing — a denominator for the falsifier below, which used to be 'counted by hand'. The fixed order still gets corrected here, in one place, permanently: a hand-set order stranded in CC's judgment became a hand-set order written down, and is now a hand-set order whose corrections are counted. Three rungs, not the top. THE NEXT RUNG, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR DONE: when /reorient lands as a parameterized gather, this skill's order becomes a per-subject SPEC that the block reads (the learning_block engine's shape — the spec carries the difference, the engine stays branchless), and the order becomes tunable against evidence instead of ruling. Owed, not built.
gates: ONE, AND IT IS NOW PHYSICS FOR THREE OF THE FOUR GATHERS (ticket the sail batch's item 1, built 2026-08-12). The seam's flat contract refuses a firing that skipped a gather, and `skills/whatslefttodo/door.py::judge_packet` RE-READS THE WORLD at the instant of firing — the gate queue, the trouble lane, the open-question lane, the newest slate — and refuses a stale figure with both numbers named. It composes each lane's own owner rather than keeping a second copy (Law 1, Law 6), and an instrument it cannot reach is a REFUSAL, never a quiet pass (Law 8). A gather that refuses is not a gather that stops you finding out: the refusal names every lack in one pass and the fix is to re-run the instrument, which was the discipline all along. WHAT IS STILL PROSE, and it is a real residue rather than a resting state: `probescan` and `test -q` are reported, not re-measured (the proof corpus costs minutes and a minutes-long judge gets routed around); and nothing detects an overview offered as a menu instead of a recommendation, which needs a reader that judges meaning.
falsifier: WRONG-INTENT if Akien has to re-order the gathers more than about twice more — that would mean the order is not a settled fact but a per-session judgment, and freezing it here was the mistake. DEAD if the /reorient parameterized gather lands and Akien stops reaching for this name — the habit was the entire justification, so no habit means no skill. RED, always, on: a gather reported without running its instrument; a truncated census presented as a population; more than one question asked per turn; the overview offered as a menu instead of a recommendation.
owner: the skills charter gates writes; Akien ratifies changes (signature gate). The ORDER of the four gathers is HIS — it is a spec-level ruling, and CC may not re-order it, add a fifth gather, or drop one without his word.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. The order of the gathers is a settled answer; re-deriving it every session is the defect this skill retires.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. Every gather names a command, and a gather reported from a record about the world is labeled as one.
Law 9 — red is the default; no triage authority. An old trouble is not stale by age, and an empty gather is a result to report, never a silent green.
founding intention learns-its-gates — the rulings gather is the training corpus for the thing that eventually stands at Akien's gate; his words: get rid of rulings 'thru learning not removal'.
idea 2026-08-11-maybe-summarize-was-the-wrong-word-we — the /reorient framing this skill is the first named subject of.
counted_by: THE SEAM, as a judged tenant — `input_contract` above is non-empty, so `cairn.machines.skill_block.skilldial` counts it via VIA_SEAM with the full efficacy set (firings, exits, refusals, and the verdicts on its findings). Before 2026-08-12 the dial said it plainly: 'declares neither an input_contract nor a counted_by … This is NOT zero uses: it is no measurement.' THE PRECEDENT THAT DOES NOT TRANSFER, checked before this was built rather than after: `cairn/machines/skill_block/counters.py` warns that giving a skill an `input_contract` to make it countable is 'the Law 1 defect wearing a helpful face' — but that warning is about a skill whose count ALREADY EXISTS somewhere else. Measured 2026-08-12: none of this skill's four instruments (recordverdict, slate, probescan, test) record their own invocations, so a firing genuinely leaves no mark anywhere, and there is no existing count to point at. The precedent transfers on the shape of the CHANGE, not on the artifact.
proof: `proofs/test_whatslefttodo.py`, built 2026-08-12 with the door — teeth on the judge, not on the prose. What they pin: the four gathers are bound to the instruments SKILL.md names; a gather reported without its instrument is refused; a count that no longer matches the live gate is refused with both numbers named; a live-trouble SET that has drifted is refused; an instrument the judge cannot reach is a refusal rather than a pass (the hollow-build tooth, Law 8); and the packet the seam accepts is exactly the packet the door accepts (one strictness, two entrances). WHAT THE PROOFS DELIBERATELY DO NOT ASSERT: any snapshot of the live world. They assert INVARIANTS against an injected measurement, because a tooth pinned to 'the gate holds 104' goes red at the moment its condition is satisfied. The four commands were each RUN and verified live on 2026-08-12 before the skill was written (recordverdict returned 104 findings; probescan returned 19 probes / 0 whole / 19 broken; test --help resolved; slate rendered the three live troubles).
provenance: Cast and built 2026-08-12, in the session that measured the 104-deep gate and the zero-disprove dial. Built FIRST, out of order, by Akien's explicit sequencing: 'and we build that first so it's out of the way and we can use it. then we go back to rulings, alarms, questions and then the slate.' Skipped ceremony, named rather than hidden: no /intent firing, no /sorted cast, no chart chain — the origin idea exists (idea 2026-08-11-maybe-summarize-was-the-wrong-word-we) and the owner ordered the build directly. That is a real gap against Law 2, recorded here so the next reader sees it instead of inferring ceremony that never ran.
